sentences: A 16-bit varying shares its 32-bit param channel with another: the producer packs them as low half, high half (Mesa `ac_nir_prerast_utils.c`: `nir_pack_32_2x16_split` by `io_sem.high_16bits`), the PS sets `FP16_INTERP_MODE` (plus `ATTR1_VALID` when the high half is used, RADV `radv_ps_input_type_bits`), and the `high` bit picks the half on both ops of the pair (ACO `emit_interp_instr`, `aco_isel_helpers.cpp`; llvm-mc gfx1013 sets the same bit, byte 5 bit 0, on both: p1ll `v2, v0, attr0.x high` 0x00 → 0x01, p2 `v2, v1, attr0.x, v3 high` 0x02 → 0x03).
The translated VS exports the channel's raw bits, so interpolating them as one f32 gives neither half.

A location any `*_f16` interp reads is therefore declared `PerVertexKHR` (`vec4[3]`, no `Flat`; it still matches a producer's vec4 output at that location); this needs `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric` (`fragmentShaderBarycentric`) for every such PS, not just the raw-barycentric ones; the index records it like any capability (`features: ["fragmentShaderBarycentric"]`), so `vk_pipeline_check` and `vk_harness` skip such a PS on a device without it.
Nothing picks `--bary-fallback` from the device: it is a translation-time flag.

Each f16 read decodes its half of each vertex's word (`UnpackHalf2x16` component 0 or 1) and weights them as AMD does, P0 + i(P1 − P0) + j(P2 − P0) with i, j = `BaryCoordKHR`.y/.z, then p2 clamps and narrows as before. f32 reads of such a location (`p1/p2_f32`) interpolate the raw word the same way, and `v_interp_mov_f32` takes vertex 0's.

Until 2026-11-22 `high` was ignored and both halves read the smooth-f32 interpolation of the whole word; abilliontokens counted `high` in 4,776 of 12,101 PS (39.5%, 51,684 instructions, always p1ll/p2 pairs, no `p1lv`), and Pipodi found 4,731 of those 4,776 read both halves of the same channel, with p1ll and p2 always agreeing on attribute, channel and `high`.
Like the f32 path, the pair's I/J operands are not read: the weights come from `BaryCoordKHR` (213 PS that compute their own barycentrics into v0/v1 first are a separate gap).

Confirmed by `tests/semantic/test_interp_f16_high.py` (per-vertex halves 0.5/1.5/2.5 and −4/8/16 at weights (0.25, 0.25, 0.5) give 1.75 and 9.0; fails on the old translation) and the GPU fixture `ps_interp_f16_high` drawn with `vs_f16_pack` (u and v packed in one channel both ways, f32 control) and, through `scripts/run_gpu_tests.py`, with the mesh producer `ms_f16_pack` (mesh `exp paramN` stores the same raw words, `Gen.ms_export`): both pass on an RTX 5070 and fail on the old translation (off by 0.984). spirv-val and `vk_pipeline_check` (real pipelines against the vec4 VS stubs, RTX 5070) also accept PS mixing high, low, f32 and flat reads of one location and of several.

**Measured natively on RDNA2** (AMD Radeon 680M, `gfx1035`, wave32 and wave64 via `tools/vinterp_hw_probe.py --oracle both`, SHADER-430): the VINTRP unit reads `P0`, `P10` and `P20` from LDS at `M0 + 48·attr + {8·c, 8·c + 4, 32 + 4·c}`; `v_interp_p1ll_f16` (and `v_interp_p1lv_f16`, taking `P0.half` from `vsrc2`) widens the selected f16 half (`[15:0]` or `[31:16]` with `high`) to binary32 and writes the fused binary32 `fma(i, f32(P10.half), f32(P0.half))`, while `v_interp_p2_f16` rounds the exact `partial_f32 + j · f32(P20.half)` once to f16 following `MODE.FP_ROUND.16_64` (like `v_fma_mixlo_f16`, whereas the translator narrows the f32 sum) and writes `vdst[15:0]` while hardware keeps `vdst[31:16]`; f16 subnormal halves are preserved with `denorm_mode_16_64 = 3` (`0x0001 + 0.5·0x0200 + 0.5·0x0200 → 0x0201`, flushed to `±0` when `0`), and f16 NaN halves quiet with payload preserved (`0x7e05 → 0x7e05`, `0x7c01 → 0x7e01`).

**ALU half measured on AMD hardware** (SHADER-430, `tools/interp_hw_probe.py`, gfx1036, every case matched; `docs/shader_validation.md`): `p1ll_f16` widens the chosen f16 halves exactly and computes fma(h10, I, h0) with one rounding to f32.
`p2_f16` computes fma(h20, J, p1ll) and rounds it once, straight to f16: 30 hand-built ties gave that result and never f32-then-f16.
The translator used to zero them and now keeps them (`write_lo16`; `test_p2_f16_keeps_the_high_half_of_vdst`).

**Still unverified:** what the SPI writes into LDS for a packed channel in a real draw (P10/P20 as f32 differences of the raw words, or per-half f16 differences under `FP16_INTERP_MODE`), which needs a pixel-shader harness; also f16 inf/NaN halves and `p1lv_f16`.
**Unverified:** AMD hardware (whether it computes P10/P20 in f16 or rounds the p1ll intermediate differently), f16 denormal and NaN halves.
**`--bary-fallback`** has no per-vertex inputs, so it keeps the old smooth-f32 read and cannot honour `high`; `check.py` skips the fixture there.
MoltenVK can't compile `PerVertexKHR`: see the next row.
